title: Telemetry scrub + runbook updates (tracing, dashboards, cost) - 2026-07-02
body:
Meeting: Observability weekly — focused scrub and runbook edits
Date: 2026-07-02 10:00-11:00 PT (compact sync)
Attendees: Maya, Ravi, Anika, Jules, Ben (brief), SRE on-call (joined 10:30)

Agenda:
- Quick metric check: token-cost + tracing volumes spike last 48h
- Dashboard clean-up: remove stale queries, unify error-rate widgets
- Sampling policy experiment: reduce full-span retention for low-cardinality services
- Runbook edits: add explicit failover steps for model variant fallback path
- Action items and owners

Summary / key takeaways:
- We confirmed a 32% rise in trace ingest for the /generate endpoint between 06/30 02:00 and 07/01 04:00 UTC, primarily tied to an opt-in A/B test that had verbose debug spans enabled (linked: JIRA OBS-4321).
- Cost telemetry shows a correlated bump in trace egress and storage cost; estimate incremental $420/day if sustained. Short-term mitigation: enable sample-rate cap for the test cohort and delete debug traces older than 72h (see quick-script below).
- Dashboards: several widgets reference deprecated label keys (model_version -> model_ver). We need a migration shim in dashboards and an update in the exporter to emit both keys for 2 weeks.
- Runbook: current failover procedure references the old model bucket. Added concrete commands and a checklist to the 'Model fallback' section. New runbook page stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Model+Fallback+Playbook

Notes to self / raw observations:
- The A/B test had sampling overridden by the dev's local config; we should add a guard to the telemetry SDK so that team-local flags cannot increase sampling beyond global max. (TODO: SDK PR)
- Strange: KV-cache hits look unchanged while tail-latency traces increased for certain traces with >1024 token sequences. Might be an interaction between tracing instrumentation and sequence-slicing logic. Add a micro-repro job.

Experiment plan: sampling-policy-2026-07-02
- Hypothesis: reducing low-value full-span retention to 5% will reduce storage cost without affecting SRE debug velocity.
- Scope: services with 95p QPS < 10k/day and label 'trace-debug=false'
- Change: set full-span-retention to 5% and keep prefix/KV spans at 20%
- Metrics to monitor: SLO alert counts, mean query latency for trace-search (es/tempo), storage growth rate, support ticket count referencing missing traces
- Rollout: canary on 'staging' for 1d, then 10% of prod traffic for 24h, then 50% if no regressions.
- Exit criteria: if any of the following within 24h: trace-search latency > +30% baseline OR missing-span incidents > 1/day OR rate of 'unable to debug' CS tickets increase.

Dashboard cleanup checklist (quick hits):
- Replace model_version with model_ver alias in all observability dashboards (dashboard ids: 214, 221, 302)
- Remove widget: 'Top 10 debug spans (last 7d)' — replace with sampled view and link to full trace query
- Add cost breakdown widget for tracing pipeline by collector/region (TS query provided in linked_artifacts)
- Create a pinned notes panel explaining sampling policy and where to find raw traces (helps CS/SEs)

Runbook edits (high-level):
- Model fallback: explicit section with commands
  - Check current model route: r-client get-route /routes/default -> confirm model_ver
  - Force fallback: r-client set-route /routes/default --model model-ver-fallback-1 --reason "observability triggered fallback"
  - Verify user-facing latency drop and monitor error budget
- Trace incident template: include checklist to verify exporter config, sampling overrides, and retention policy
- Add 'cost spike' play: immediate throttling knobs, sample-rate reduction, and emergency retention purge script (location: /ops/scripts/trace-purge.sh)

Action items (owner / due):
- Ravi: SDK guard PR to cap local sampling overrides (JIRA OBS-4398) — Due: 2026-07-09
- Anika: Dashboard migration shim + update dashboard ids 214,221,302 — Due: 2026-07-06
- Jules: Implement canary rollout for sampling-policy-2026-07-02 and run staging test — Due: 2026-07-04
- Maya: Draft runbook 'Model Fallback' and cost-spike play; add step-by-step commands and slack escalation flow — Due: 2026-07-03
- Ben (SRE): Schedule micro-repro job for sequence-slicing interaction and attach logs to OBS-4321 — Due: 2026-07-05

Quick mitigations executed during meeting:
- Reduced sampling for the A/B test cohort from 100% -> 10% (immediate)
- Ran a retention purge on debug traces older than 72h for the affected namespace (manual script, ~6.2GB freed)
- Temporary alert mute added to reduce noise while canary proceeds (alert ids: a-1102, a-1105)

Open questions / unresolved:
- How do we balance developer-level debug ability with org-wide cost constraints? Propose a quota system per team with an override path for critical debug sessions.
- Is there a cheaper storage tier we can stream cold traces into (S3 Glacier-like) for long tail historical debugging? Reach out to infra-cost team for options.
- Need to validate whether tracing instrumentation affects sequence-slicing perf; if yes, consider moving heavy-span creation onto an async path.

Follow-ups for next sync (2026-07-09):
- Results from staging canary for sampling policy
- Dashboard migration progress and preview link
- Updated runbook published and reviewed by SRE/Support
- Cost delta after purge and sampling change (early estimate for 72h window)

Appendix: quick-script used during purge (for reference)
- curl -X POST https://telemetry-api.redwood.ai/admin/purge -d '{\"namespace\":\"test-ab-cohort-12\",\"older_than_hours\":72,\"span_type\":\"debug\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>'

Random notes / scratch:
- Might add a lightweight "telemetry-budget" label to projects so billing can be attributed at team level.
- Reminder: add a one-pager and a short demo for GTM to explain tracing cost controls (product asked for this).

End of notes.
